readings.title: The Sin Offering for the Priest and Assembly
readings.subtitle: Unintentional Sins of the Anointed and the Congregation
readings.text: [Leviticus 4:1] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying, [2] <dq>“Speak to the children of Yisra’ĕl, saying, ‘When a being sins by mistake against any of the commands of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> regarding things which should not be done, and shall do any of them:</dq> [3] <dq>‘If the anointed priest sins, bringing guilt on the people, then he shall bring to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> for his sin which he has sinned a young bull, a perfect one, for a sin offering.</dq> [4] <dq>‘And he shall bring the bull to the door of the Tent of Meeting before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and lay his hand on the bull’s head, and slaughter the bull before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [5] <dq>‘And the anointed priest shall take some of the bull’s blood and bring it to the Tent of Meeting.</dq> [6] <dq>‘And the priest shall dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle some of the blood seven times before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, in front of the veil of the Set-apart Place.</dq> [7] <dq>‘And the priest shall put some of the blood on the horns of the altar of sweet incense before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, which is in the Tent of Meeting. And he shall pour all the rest of the blood of the bull at the base of the altar of the burnt offering, which is at the door of the Tent of Meeting.</dq> [8] <dq>‘And he takes all the fat of the bull as the sin offering: the fat that covers the entrails and all the fat which is on the entrails,</dq> [9] <dq>and the two kidneys and the fat that is on them by the loins, and the appendage on the liver, which he removes with the kidneys,</dq> [10] <dq>as it was taken from the bull of the slaughtering of peace offerings. And the priest shall burn them on the altar of the burnt offering.</dq> [11] <dq>‘But the skin of the bull, and all its flesh, with its head and with its legs, and its entrails and its dung,</dq> [12] <dq>he shall bring out the whole bull to the outside of the camp to a clean place, where the ashes are poured out, and burn it on wood with fire. Where the ashes are poured out it is burned.</dq> [13] <dq>‘And if the entire congregation of Yisra’ĕl strays by mistake, and the matter has been hidden from the eyes of the assembly, and they have done against any of the commands of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> regarding things which should not be done, and are guilty,</dq> [14] <dq>when the sin which they have sinned becomes known, then the assembly shall bring a young bull for the sin, and bring it before the Tent of Meeting.</dq> [15] <dq>‘And the elders of the congregation shall lay their hands on the head of the bull before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and the bull shall be slaughtered before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [16] <dq>‘And the anointed priest shall bring some of the bull’s blood to the Tent of Meeting.</dq> [17] <dq>‘And the priest shall dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle it seven times before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, in front of the veil.</dq> [18] <dq>‘And he puts some of the blood on the horns of the altar which is before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, which is in the Tent of Meeting. And he pours all the rest of the blood at the base of the altar of burnt offering, which is at the door of the Tent of Meeting.</dq> [19] <dq>‘And he takes all the fat from it and shall burn it on the altar.</dq> [20] <dq>‘And he shall do with the bull as he did with the bull as a sin offering, so he does with it. And the priest shall make atonement for them, and it shall be forgiven them.</dq> [21] <dq>‘And he shall bring out the bull to the outside of the camp and burn it as he burned the first bull. It is a sin offering for the assembly.</dq>

readings.title: The Sin Offering for Rulers and Common People
readings.subtitle: Unintentional Sins of Leaders and Individuals
readings.text: [Leviticus 4:22] <dq>‘When a ruler sins, and by mistake does against any of the commands of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> his <dn>Elohim</dn> regarding things which should not be done, and is guilty,</dq> [23] <dq>or if his sin which he has sinned is made known to him, then he shall bring as his offering a buck of the goats, a male, a perfect one.</dq> [24] <dq>‘And he shall lay his hand on the head of the goat, and slaughter it at the place where they slaughter the burnt offering before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. It is a sin offering.</dq> [25] <dq>‘And the priest shall take some of the blood of the sin offering with his finger, and put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering, and pour its blood at the base of the altar of burnt offering.</dq> [26] <dq>‘And he burns all its fat on the altar, like the fat of the slaughtering of the peace offerings. And the priest shall make atonement for him concerning his sin, and it shall be forgiven him.</dq> [27] <dq>‘And if any being of the people of the land sins by mistake by doing against any of the commands of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> regarding things which should not be done, and is guilty,</dq> [28] <dq>or if his sin which he has sinned is made known to him, then he shall bring as his offering a kid of the goats, a female, a perfect one, for his sin which he has sinned.</dq> [29] <dq>‘And he shall lay his hand on the head of the sin offering, and slaughter the sin offering at the place of the burnt offering.</dq> [30] <dq>‘And the priest shall take some of its blood with his finger, and put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering, and pour all the rest of the blood at the base of the altar.</dq> [31] <dq>‘And he removes all its fat, as fat is removed from the slaughtering of the peace offerings. And the priest shall burn it on the altar for a sweet fragrance to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And the priest shall make atonement for him, and it shall be forgiven him.</dq> [32] <dq>‘And if he brings a lamb as his sin offering, he brings a female, a perfect one.</dq> [33] <dq>‘And he shall lay his hand on the head of the sin offering, and slaughter it as a sin offering at the place where they slaughter the burnt offering.</dq> [34] <dq>‘And the priest shall take some of the blood of the sin offering with his finger, and put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering, and pour all the rest of the blood at the base of the altar.</dq> [35] <dq>‘And he removes all its fat, as the fat of the lamb is removed from the slaughtering of the peace offerings. And the priest shall burn them on the altar, according to the offerings made by fire to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And the priest shall make atonement for him for his sin that he has sinned, and it shall be forgiven him.</dq>

readings.title: Specific Sins Requiring Offerings
readings.subtitle: Witnessing, Uncleanliness, and Rash Oaths
readings.text: [Leviticus 5:1] <dq>‘And when a being sins in that he hears the voice of swearing, and is a witness, or has seen, or has known, and does not declare it, then he bears his perversity.</dq> [2] <dq>‘Or when a being touches any unclean matter, or the carcass of an unclean beast, or the carcass of unclean livestock, or the carcass of unclean creeping creatures, and it has been hidden from him, he is unclean and guilty.</dq> [3] <dq>‘Or when he touches the uncleanness of man, any of his uncleanness by which he is unclean, and it has been hidden from him, when he knows it, then he is guilty.</dq> [4] <dq>‘Or when a being swears, speaking rashly with his lips to do evil or to do good, whatever it is that a man speaks rashly with an oath, and it has been hidden from him, when he knows it, then he is guilty in one of these.</dq> [5] <dq>‘And it shall be, when he is guilty in one of these, that he shall confess that in which he has sinned.</dq> [6] <dq>‘And he shall bring his guilt offering to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> for his sin which he has sinned, a female from the flock, a lamb or a kid of the goats as a sin offering. And the priest shall make atonement for him, for his sin.</dq> [7] <dq>‘And if he is unable to bring a lamb, then he shall bring to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> for his trespass which he has committed, two turtledoves or two young pigeons, one for a sin offering and the other for a burnt offering.</dq> [8] <dq>‘And he shall bring them to the priest, who shall bring that which is for the sin offering first, and pinch off its head at the back of its neck, but shall not sever it.</dq> [9] <dq>‘And he shall sprinkle some of the blood of the sin offering on the side of the altar, and the rest of the blood shall be drained out at the base of the altar. It is a sin offering.</dq> [10] <dq>‘And he prepares the second as a burnt offering according to the right ruling. And the priest shall make atonement for him, for his sin which he has sinned, and it shall be forgiven him.</dq> [11] <dq>‘But if he is unable to bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons, then he who sinned shall bring for his offering one-tenth of an ĕphah of fine flour as a sin offering. He puts no oil on it, nor does he put frankincense on it, for it is a sin offering.</dq> [12] <dq>‘And he shall bring it to the priest, and the priest shall take his handful of it as a remembrance portion, and burn it on the altar according to the offerings made by fire to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. It is a sin offering.</dq> [13] <dq>‘And the priest shall make atonement for him, for his sin that he has sinned in any of these, and it shall be forgiven him. And it shall be the priest’s, like the grain offering.’ ”</dq>

readings.title: Trespass Offerings
readings.subtitle: Unintentional Trespass in Set-apart Matters
readings.text: [Leviticus 5:14] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying, [15] <dq>“When a being commits a trespass, and sins by mistake against the set-apart matters of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, then he shall bring to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> his guilt offering, a ram, a perfect one, from the flock, with your valuation in shekels of silver according to the shekel of the set-apart place, as a guilt offering.</dq> [16] <dq>“And he shall make good for the sin that he has done against that which is set-apart, and shall add one-fifth to it and give it to the priest. And the priest shall make atonement for him with the ram of the guilt offering, and it shall be forgiven him.</dq> [17] <dq>“And if a being sins, and does any of the commands of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> regarding things which should not be done, though he did not know it, yet he is guilty and shall bear his perversity.</dq> [18] <dq>“And he shall bring to the priest a ram, a perfect one, from the flock, with your valuation, as a guilt offering. And the priest shall make atonement for him for his mistake which he committed, though he did not know it, and it shall be forgiven him.</dq> [19] <dq>“It is a guilt offering, he was truly guilty before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.”</dq>

readings.title: Trespass Against a Neighbor
readings.subtitle: Restitution and Atonement
readings.text: [Leviticus 6:1] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying, [2] <dq>“When a being sins and commits a trespass against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and has lied to his neighbor about a deposit, or about a pledge, or about a robbery, or has extorted from his neighbor,</dq> [3] <dq>or has found what was lost and lies concerning it, and swears falsely – so that he sins regarding any of these things that a man does –</dq> [4] <dq>then it shall be, because he has sinned and is guilty, that he shall restore what he has stolen, or the thing which he has extorted, or what was delivered to him to keep, or the lost thing which he found,</dq> [5] <dq>or all that about which he has sworn falsely. He shall restore its full value, add one-fifth more to it, and give it to whomever it belongs, on the day of his guilt offering.</dq> [6] <dq>“And he brings his guilt offering to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, a ram, a perfect one, from the flock, with your valuation, as a guilt offering, to the priest.</dq> [7] <dq>“And the priest shall make atonement for him before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and he shall be forgiven for whatever he has done to be guilty.”</dq>

readings.title: The Law of the Burnt Offering
readings.subtitle: Instructions for the Priests
readings.text: [Leviticus 6:8] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying, [9] <dq>“Command Aharon and his sons, saying, ‘This is the Torah of the burnt offering: The burnt offering is on the hearth on the altar all night until morning, and the fire of the altar is kept burning on it.</dq> [10] <dq>‘And the priest shall put on his linen garment, and his linen trousers he puts on his body, and take up the ashes of the burnt offering which the fire has consumed on the altar, and he shall put them beside the altar.</dq> [11] <dq>‘And he shall take off his garments, and put on other garments, and bring the ashes outside the camp to a clean place.</dq> [12] <dq>‘And the fire on the altar is kept burning on it, it is not put out. And the priest shall burn wood on it every morning, and arrange the burnt offering on it, and shall burn on it the fat of the peace offerings.</dq> [13] <dq>‘Fire shall be kept burning continually on the altar; it is not put out.</dq>

readings.title: The Law of the Grain Offering
readings.subtitle: Portions for the Priests
readings.text: [Leviticus 6:14] <dq>‘And this is the Torah of the grain offering: The sons of Aharon shall bring it before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, in front of the altar.</dq> [15] <dq>‘And he shall take from it his handful of the fine flour of the grain offering, with its oil, and all the frankincense which is on the grain offering, and shall burn it on the altar for a sweet fragrance, as a remembrance portion to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [16] <dq>‘And the rest of it Aharon and his sons eat – unleavened it is eaten in a set-apart place, in the courtyard of the Tent of Meeting they eat it.</dq> [17] <dq>‘It is not baked with leaven. <dn>I</dn> have given it as their portion of <dn>My</dn> offerings made by fire. It is most set-apart, like the sin offering and the guilt offering.</dq> [18] <dq>‘All the males among the children of Aharon eat it. It is a law forever in your generations concerning the offerings made by fire to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. Everyone who touches them becomes set-apart.’ ”</dq>

readings.title: The Offering of the Priest
readings.subtitle: The Daily Grain Offering
readings.text: [Leviticus 6:19] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying, [20] <dq>“This is the offering of Aharon and his sons, which they bring to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, beginning on the day when he is anointed: one-tenth of an ĕphah of fine flour as a daily grain offering, half of it in the morning and half of it at night.</dq> [21] <dq>“It is made on a griddle with oil. You bring it in mixed, pieces of the grain offering baked, you bring as a sweet fragrance to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [22] <dq>“And the priest from among his sons, who is anointed in his place, prepares it. It is a law forever to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. It is entirely burned.</dq> [23] <dq>“And every grain offering for the priest is entirely burned, it is not eaten.”</dq>

readings.title: The Law of the Sin Offering
readings.subtitle: Holiness of the Offering
readings.text: [Leviticus 6:24] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying, [25] <dq>“Speak to Aharon and to his sons, saying, ‘This is the Torah of the sin offering: In the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered, the sin offering is slaughtered before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. It is most set-apart.</dq> [26] <dq>‘The priest who brings it for sin eats it. In a set-apart place it is eaten, in the courtyard of the Tent of Meeting.</dq> [27] <dq>‘Everyone who touches its flesh becomes set-apart. And when its blood is sprinkled on any garment, you wash that on which it was sprinkled in a set-apart place.</dq> [28] <dq>‘But the earthen vessel in which it is boiled is broken. And if it is boiled in a bronze pot, it is scoured and rinsed in water.</dq> [29] <dq>‘All the males among the priests eat it. It is most set-apart.</dq> [30] <dq>‘But no sin offering from which any of the blood is brought into the Tent of Meeting, to make atonement in the Set-apart Place, is eaten, it is burned with fire.</dq>
